question: Can a list join / meet-in-the-middle lower the r7 row?
number: No split: after one full round every digest word depends on every input and every CV word (strict avalanche 0.500 from round 2, heur_test.json), so neither a prefix-condition join (K0 couples two functions of the same P) nor a state-meet join exists. Round-0 table route: round 0 is 2614 gates = 5.7 % of the step, upper bound 0.084 bit if free, but each diagonal call needs a table of 2^64 entries (64-bit message pair): memory term +44 bits or more, bit-sliced lanes have no random access. Birthday list join: needs 2^128 memory, memoryless rho is already the optimum (Q = 1.036 x 2^128).
source: main session 10-17 b3_tech dig: minutes-scale exact gate counts and numpy tests
notes: Round range: dead r3..r7 (round-0 share falls 0.237 -> 0.084 bit, table size fixed at 2^64 per call).

object: BLAKE3 pareto layer r7 x technique sym
question: Does a rotational, complement or word-permutation symmetry of the r7 compression give an orbit search?
number: Equivariance test, 32768 random x: HD(f(T x), U f(x)) mean 127.9..128.1 (min 90..99) for T in rot1, rot8, rot16, complement, word cyclic shift, pair swap, at every R = 1..7: no symmetry. Reason: IV words (v0..v3 and v8..v11) and length/flags are not rotation- or permutation-invariant, so a symmetric pair never maps to a symmetric pair; orbit search would save only 0.5 bit per halving of the range.

notes: Dead r1..r7 (tested), same as the grid cells for 2 rounds (X: row 2 is IV).
